expectations.text: Rejects redefining `full_access` and states scopes are additive-only, never repurposed.
expectations.evidence: 'Do not redefine `full_access`.' and 'Additive-only, forever.'

expectations.text: Explains that repurposing silently changes what already-granted consents authorize.
expectations.evidence: 'Existing grants and live tokens currently authorize read and write ... `full_access` means two things depending on grant date.'

expectations.text: Notes that scope-set changes invalidate refresh tokens and force re-consent, so the redefinition does not actually avoid touching the existing registrations.
expectations.evidence: Only says moving to new scopes 'is a new grant and needs consent'; no refresh-token invalidation point.

expectations.text: Rejects deferring the token-type binding and requires every scope bound to a token type (app identity versus user delegation) on day one.
expectations.evidence: 'Do not defer the integration/user token split. Bind every scope to a token type now.'

expectations.text: States the documented cost of deferring it: changing a scope's token-type binding later requires reauthorization from every user.
expectations.evidence: Slack documents that changing the binding later 'requires reauthorization from every user'.

expectations.text: Recommends `resource:action` naming as the default granularity rung.
expectations.evidence: '**Naming:** `resource:action`'.

expectations.text: Requires a read/write split with read-only as the default.
expectations.evidence: Read/write split present, but no read-only default is stated.

expectations.text: Names scopes after the same resource nouns the API already uses (`projects`, `tasks`, `comments`, `timesheets`).
expectations.evidence: '`projects`, `tasks`, `comments`, `timesheets`'.

expectations.text: Treats the single broad catch-all scope as a deleted anti-pattern rather than a coarse tier worth keeping in the menu.
expectations.evidence: 'Never create a single broad catch-all scope. No `full_write`.'

expectations.text: Positions fine-grained per-resource permissions as the starved option, promoted only on named conditions such as admin approval policies, a compliance regime, or scopes reaching org-wide data.
expectations.evidence: Not discussed.

expectations.text: Warns that a migration to fine-grained permissions is lossy in edge-case coverage, so the coarser tier stays alive during the transition instead of a hard cutover.
expectations.evidence: 'GitHub's fine-grained model "cannot accomplish every task" ... do not force a lossy cutover.'
